social isolation and loneliness increase the risk of depression and probably also anxiety.
social isolation and loneliness are associated with an increased risk of depression in children and adolescents, both during isolation and in the future.
social isolation and loneliness increase the risk of depression and probably increase the risk of anxiety at the time of loneliness and between 0-9 years later in healthy children and young people.

the impact of social distancing and isolation on the mental health and well-being of children, adolescents and families in the UK.
the effects of social isolation and social distancing measures, such as school closures and social distancing on children's and adolescents' mental health.
the mental health of children and young people during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact on the mental wellbeing of young people.

children and adolescents who are isolated are more likely to have depression and probably anxiety.

children and adolescents are more likely to experience mental health problems if they are lonely and/or isolated, and this risk is increased during and after a disease containment measure such as social distancing.

children and adolescents are more likely to experience depression and possibly anxiety during and after isolation ends.
